items.title: Pigeons Playing Ping Pong- Jeremy Schon & Greg Ormont interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, March 8, 2024
items.q: we all listen to a lot of instrumental music, especially like kind of groove-oriented instrumental music you know like people like John Scofield more in the jazz world.

ctx.x: Well when I listen to the song “Horizon” which you’ve been doing what for ten years now, it’s got that beautiful vamp in the beginning with those two guitar lines and it lasts a long time. And you’re not really — this of course is just my opinion — you’re not really jamming, you’re playing this thing for 32 bars or whatever, and when you recorded that did you feel like it doesn’t need anything more than that, we’re just going to do that for quite some time and then we’re going to add something on top of it and do…

You’ve cracked the code. I mean we’ve, as a band you know and as individual people, we’ve always, I mean we all listen to a lot of instrumental music, especially like kind of groove-oriented instrumental music you know like people like John Scofield more in the jazz world. And like we love to be able to vamp on a cool groove. If there’s anything that, you know, for “Horizon” I feel like we thought all right, the simple guitar melody that’s happening is very simple, but it catchy enough. And I don’t know, somehow…

And in those instances you know, like Jeremy wrote the bulk of that song and when he does he’ll send them my way usually or I’ll be sitting next to him in college or whatever the time period is. And I’ll think about adding vocals, almost always, where we sing often. We have a lot of instrumentals but the majority have vocals. And the intro I ended up, you know coming across this like idea, and the song kind of harkened me back to some other concerts I’ve been to where there’s a vamp that’s building and you kind…
